note: NOT a crash predicate -- nothing about this issue is crash-shaped, and dxc itself compiles every one of these shaders successfully with exit 0. The symptom is purely in the metadata the PIX 'numbering' pass (-dxil-annotate-with-virtual-regs) writes, so the predicate is scored over check-2923.py's report of that metadata rather than over a dxc diagnostic. `nonzero_exit` would be meaningless here: every stage exits 0 in both the good and the bad case. The marker fires when the pass allocates a PIX virtual-register range for a source variable (or a DW_OP_bit_piece fragment of one) via llvm.dbg.declare and then records no !pix-alloca-reg-write against any register in that range -- i.e. the registers PIX would read for that variable are numbered somewhere the member writes were not. That is the observable form of 'the numbering pass got confused about offsets of members'. Controls: control-no-subroutine.hlsl is PixTest.cpp's PixStructAnnotation_SequentialFloatN shader verbatim, which the test asserts is numbered correctly -- it must NOT match (captured at -Od and -O1). control-inout-param.hlsl is repro.hlsl with the single word `inout` added, so the subroutine gets a pointer instead of a copy -- it must NOT match either, which is what isolates the by-value struct copy rather than 'calling a subroutine' as the trigger. A weaker predicate was rejected: 'the modified unit test fails' also fires on control-inout-param.hlsl (its single alloca ends up with two dbg.declare users, so FindStructMemberFromStore rejects every store and AllocaWrites comes back empty), which would have made the predicate match a case whose register numbering is in fact self-consistent. check-2923.py's own emulation of the unit test's assertions is still printed, as supporting evidence, but it is deliberately not what is matched on. check-2923.py also prints PIX-2923: PARSE-WARNING if any llvm.dbg.declare in the module could not be attributed to an annotated alloca; that guard exists because the first version of its dbg.declare regex could not match a '[1 x float]*' operand and silently reported the reproducing case as clean.
